title: Engagement trajectory: deck + playbook (Standard & Enterprise)
abstract: Working draft: two variant QBR decks + an actionable playbook and lightweight renewal tracker. Purpose: give CSMs a repeatable narrative that aligns usage signals to business outcomes, surface risk earlier, and create a clear path to renewal across both Standard and Enterprise accounts.
slide_outline: Cover — Partnership trajectory (logo, account name, CSM, date)
Executive snapshot — topline health, NRR signal, renewal date, recommended motion (Standard | Enterprise)
Business outcomes — customer goals we map to model/feature usage (3 bullets)
Usage & adoption trends — tokens/requests by product area, 90/30/7 day change
Quality & regressions — evals summary, recent failures and mitigations
Reliability & SLOs — latency P50/P95, error rate, incidents since last QBR
Value realized — examples of reductions in latency/cost or feature launches enabled by Redwood
Roadmap alignment — upcoming features and how they help customer goals
Renewal posture & options — recommended renewal tier, upsell targets, timing
Risks & asks — open blockers, legal/compliance items, exec escalations needed
Next steps & owners — concrete 30/60/90 day plan with owners and success metrics
speaker_notes: Cover: quick context callout — who is in the room, primary success metric to track for this account.
Executive snapshot: one-sentence health summary first (green/yellow/red), then 3 lines of evidence (usage, SLOs, sentiment). For Enterprise add contract cadence and primary stakeholder list.

Business outcomes: map each outcome to a measurable metric we can track post-renewal (e.g., reduce end-user latency by 50ms, cut inference cost by 30%). Keep language customer-first ("they care about...").

Usage slide: call out anomalies and explain steps taken (query patterns, model swaps, caching). Use small charts; avoid dumping raw logs. For Standard accounts keep it high level; for Enterprise include per-route token breakdown.
Quality & regressions: show two representative prompts and how outputs changed. If regressions found, include test-set score before/after remediation.
SLOs: surface both platform SLOs and contract SLOs. If we missed an SLA, explain impact and compensating actions.
Value realized: present a short case study inside the account — time-to-value with dates, outcome achieved, and testimonial quote if available.
Roadmap: focus on 1-2 items that materially affect the customer's roadmap. For Enterprise include ETA and supported migration path.
Renewal posture: propose options (auto-renew, 12/24 month committed capacity, dedicated GPU pool). Tie each option to expected unit economics.
Risks & asks: be explicit — e.g., legal needs SOC2 paperwork, security requires VPC peering, product needs access to sample prompts. Assign names and deadlines.
Next steps: always close with the next meeting date, who will send the contract draft or PoC plan, and the single metric we will reconvene on.
playbook_steps: Pre-QBR (3 weeks): pull metrics, run 5 canonical prompts, refresh evals, pre-send 'agenda & asks' email
Pre-QBR (1 week): calibrate slides with solutions & product (validation of any fixes), prep renewal options and commercial contours
QBR meeting: start with executive snapshot, spend 15 minutes on outcomes, 20 on adoption and risks, 10 on renewal motion
Immediate follow-up (24-72h): send meeting notes, assign owners for each ask, share contract/POC artifacts
30/60 day cadence: track the metric we committed to, weekly sync for Enterprise accounts with open remediation workstreams
Escalation: if risk_score <= 30 and >7 days no mitigation, escalate to CS lead + AE; if risk_score <= 10, exec alert and legal loop-in
risk_scoring_rubric: Scale 1-100 (lower = higher risk). Combine: usage velocity (40%), SLO breaches (30%), sentiment & support volume (20%), commercial signals (10%).
Score buckets: 0-20 critical, 21-40 high, 41-70 medium, 71-100 low
Example: account with ramping error rate (+SLO breaches) and paused procurement would fall into 15-25 range -> high/critical
checklist: Confirm renewal date in CRM and update tracker
Run canonical prompt suite and attach outputs to the deck
Validate any recent incident RCA included
Prepare 2 renewal options (term + committed capacity) with pricing range
For Enterprise: ensure legal & security packet is attached and named owner is present
escalation_matrix: Primary CSM -> CS Manager -> Head of Customer Success -> VP GTM. Include AE and Legal depending on commercial/legal blockers. For data/privacy blockers add Security lead. Put expected SLAs for each escalation (24h for Manager, 72h for Head).
appendix: Templates included: 1) One-page executive snapshot PDF; 2) Slide master (light / dark); 3) CSV renewal tracker; 4) Example exec email. Stored in drive: /shared_drives/customer-success/templates. If you need a custom Enterprise pricing sketch ping finance: fin-account-pricing@redwood.ai
